item.text: I’ll inspect the service documentation first, then build a small read-only reconciliation script outside the workspace, handle token refresh/rate limits, and validate the exact `result.json` shape and totals before handing it over.

item.aggregated_output:
Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

item.text: The docs confirm pagination is 50 orders per page, authentication is bearer-token based, and customer records provide the region and whole-number discount. I’m now fetching every page with retry-on-rate-limit/error behavior, deduplicating by order ID before applying the UTC/status/date rules, and caching each customer lookup.

The full listing completed successfully: 30 pages, 1,480 unique listed orders, and 20 duplicate listings skipped. The qualifying set contains 407 distinct shipped orders; I’m writing the requested artifact now and then checking its keys, JSON validity, and arithmetic.

assert all(isinstance(data[k], int) for k in ('total_cents', 'order_count', 'duplicates_skipped'))

assert sum(data['by_region'].values()) == data['total_cents']

print('region_sum=', sum(data['by_region'].values()))
